A mixed-format dataset example lists KML, orthophoto tiles, panoramic imagery, and other attached resources.
A KML flight-planning centerline appears in a map viewer screenshot.
An Open Aerial Map screenshot shows the orthophoto over the map and the resource details.
A Google Street View slide shows a 360-degree aerial panorama and its link.
Depositar recent updates lists Google Dataset Search, the citation tool, outreach, policy, and workshop activities.
Google Dataset Search results show the coral reef soundscapes dataset and its Depositar link.
FAIRness of Research Data on depositar introduces F-UJI and its automated FAIR assessment.
A F-UJI assessment summary presents the selected river dataset, its 47 percent score, and the four FAIR dimension scores.
The detailed F-UJI Findable report lists individual metrics and highlights the persistent identifier criterion.
Depositar’s work in progress includes ARK identifiers, homepage design, CoreTrustSeal, and audiovisual uploads.
The closing slide shows the repository, documentation and source links, the contact address, and project acknowledgments.
Conference introduction adds the full talk title, speaker, and date.
Speaker title slide identifies QPS BV and the FOSS4G Europe Mostar venue.
Takeaway slide contrasts hydrographic and terrestrial data and introduces Boost.Geometry for adapting legacy code.
Agenda lists hydrographic data, adapting existing C++ types, and a demonstration.
Bathymetry slide explains multibeam echo soundings and shows a vessel measuring the seabed.
Hydrographic error-model slide covers sound-speed and positioning errors and nuisance signals, with beam geometry diagrams.
Hydrographic data volume tables compare points per second and points per square meter at three depths.
Legacy codebase slide gives the approximate code size and age and its C++, C, and C# mix.
Boost.Geometry slide introduces provided adapters, concepts, and custom adapters.
Concepts slide lists supported geometries and illustrates Point, Linestring, and Ring/Polygon.
Macro adaptation slide shows C++ structs and Boost.Geometry registration macros for a point and box.
Hydrographic point storage slide describes keeping pings grouped and replacing bespoke quad-tree lookups with a Boost.Geometry R-tree.
Keeping pings coherent slide illustrates oriented bounding boxes and explains adapting the box concept.
The concepts implementation slide shows C++ trait specializations and indexed access for an oriented bounding box.
Specializing algorithms slide shows an indexability trait and a custom intersection specialization.
Building and querying an index slide shows the R-tree declaration, population, and intersection query.
The presentation returns to the Takeaway content for the conclusion.
Future Work slide proposes an oriented bounding box concept and asks for mentorship.
State of Ocean Mapping slide shows the Seabed 2030 update and its 27.3 percent coverage figure.
QPS closing slide shows the company’s closing message against an aerial ocean image.
The conference card returns with the talk title, speaker, date, and livestream sponsor.
The opening-style FOSS4G conference and Powered by OSGeo credit card returns.

boundary_evidence.description: SITICOM introduction shows the company’s transformation and network service areas.
Agenda introduces DuckDB, comparisons, data retrieval, input and export, the spatial extension, an example, and QGIS.
DuckDB usage slide lists installation, CLI and language integrations, browser execution, extensions, and single-file storage.
DuckDB details slide describes an in-process, column-oriented analytical database, multithreading, and local or remote data.
Database comparison places SQLite, DuckDB, PostgreSQL, and ClickHouse on in-process versus client/server and OLTP versus OLAP axes.
PostgreSQL/PostGIS comparison covers its client/server, multiuser, and permissions model and established geospatial integrations.
OGR2OGR comparison describes GDAL’s raster and vector support, format conversion, and filtering.
SQLite/GeoPackage comparison covers file-based storage, transactions, and GeoPackage support.
Dataframes comparison discusses R, pandas, GeoPandas, and in-process DuckDB integrations.
Modern SQL slide shows alternative SELECT syntax, DESCRIBE, EXCLUDE, and reading a CSV during table creation.
Database creation slide shows the DuckDB CLI invocation and explains persisted tables and remote views.
Input Data slide lists file formats, databases, text files, and spatial inputs.
CSV slide shows a direct SQL read, type and column-name inference, and a sample CSV.
Parquet slide compares columnar storage, compression, and HTTP range reads and mentions GeoParquet.
Data Export slide shows a SQL COPY example above a photo of ducks on the water.
DuckDB Spatial introduction gives the release context, supported libraries, and spatial limitations.
Airport example introduces the number-of-airports-per-country question with a map of airport points.
Example Query slide shows the spatial join, count query, and literal CSV result.
QGIS Plugin slide introduces QDuckDB and its DuckDB read support.
Conclusion highlights DuckDB’s installation, analysis and conversion use cases, multiuser limitations, and ecosystem.
Links slide collects DuckDB, DuckDB Spatial, playground, and reference links.
The browser-based DuckDB shell opens to a ready prompt and an in-memory database.
The .help command prints the DuckDB web shell command list and related links.
The .examples command prints remote Parquet scan and join examples. The first rows appear beside the camera inset and the later scroll exposes the full example.
The remote customer Parquet count query finishes and its result table appears. The camera inset initially covers the value, which is visible later.
The feed returns to the Links slide in the browser PDF viewer after the DuckDB shell demonstration.
Conference end card thanks its sponsors and displays their names and logos.

COPY (
    SELECT
        country_name,
        count(*) AS count
    FROM
        (
            SELECT
                a.name AS airport_name,
                c.name AS country_name
            FROM
                ST_Read (
                    'data/natural_earth_vector.gpkg',
                    layer = 'ne_10m_airports'
                ) AS a
            JOIN ST_Read ('data/countries/ne_10m_admin_0_countries.shp') AS c
            ON st_within(a.geom, c.geom)
        )
    GROUP BY
        country_name
    ORDER BY
        count DESC
) TO 'results.csv';

boundary_evidence.description: Conference title card adds the talk title, Jin Igarashi, July 18, 2025, and the GeoCat livestream sponsor.
Jin Igarashi bio with his UNDP role, University of Leeds degree, GIS for Water and UNDP GeoHub projects.
mapbox-gl-draw slide explains its use for drawing in Mapbox and MapLibre and documents issues with MapLibre.
Terra Draw diagram shows the unified drawing API and adapters for six map libraries.
More details about Terra Draw slide links to James Milner’s conference talk and shows its event listing.
What is maplibre-gl-terradraw? section opener.
What controls are available? diagram presents the drawing and measurement controls with their roles.
What features are available? table lists drawing and editing modes and marks the plugin’s own modes.
Motivation to develop the plugin slide lists the integration work for buttons, icons and map-library support.
Get yourself started slide shows where to choose a control and its modes.
Simple installation slide shows JavaScript imports, map setup and the call that adds the drawing control.
Map screenshot points out the plugin’s preconfigured toolbar icons and buttons.
Measuring distance, area and elevation section opener.
Measure control slide shows JavaScript configuring the measurement control, units, precision and elevation.
Returns to the Simple installation JavaScript slide.
Returns to the Measure control JavaScript slide after the brief map-slide flash.
Example map shows point elevation, line distance and elevation, polygon area, and measurement settings.
Dynamic altitude diagram connects the plugin, @watergis/terrain-rgb and raster DEM tiles, with an AWS Terrain Tiles example.
Bring your own raster-dem shows a custom TerrainRGB tile configuration and a Rwanda elevation map.
Access to Terra Draw API shows getTerraDrawInstance() and how to supply a GeoJSON feature.
Terra Draw API documentation index and list of available modules.
Examples slide shows the gallery of sample maps and use cases.
Live demo slide supplies the demo URL and QR code.
The live demo settles on Default Control with the drawing toolbar and blue sample shapes.
Measure Control is active and the sample map shows readable distance, elevation and area measurements.
A newly placed point in Ireland displays its altitude beside the existing point.
The new multisegment line across Central Asia has its final shape, distance and vertex elevations.
A newly drawn polygon over Central and South Asia displays its settled area measurement.
Delete all leaves the measurement map clear of geometry and measurement labels.
The new rectangle over central and eastern Europe settles with its area label.
The newly drawn circle over north-central Africa settles with its area label.
The closed polygon covering part of the Arabian Peninsula and Iran settles with an area label.
The angled rectangle over Central Asia remains in place after its drawing cursor leaves the corner. The result is visible before area labels begin appearing.
The placed angled rectangle gains its final area readout, 1751745.35 km².
The sensor-shaped sector off northwestern Africa settles with its area measurement.
The drawn sector over northern India settles with its final area label.
Selecting the circle reveals its editing handles and readable selected-feature GeoJSON.
The selected circle settles in its new position and displays a revised area.
The vertex edit leaves a persistent pointed extension on the circle’s upper-right edge and changes its displayed area.
Selecting the edited circle displays updated GeoJSON coordinates.
Delete selection removes the edited circle while the other features remain.
Delete all clears the other measured features from the map.
Mode Selection opens the persistent configuration panel with the active modes and bulk actions.
Deleting all enabled modes removes the drawing toolbar and leaves the empty selection configuration.
Adding all modes restores the full toolbar and labeled sample geometries.
Clearing the mode selection again leaves an unannotated map without drawing tools.
The polygon-only configuration shows the polygon button and its sample geometries.
The selected polygon, linestring and point modes produce a three-button toolbar and their sample geometry.
Adding delete creates a four-mode configuration with a delete button and reloaded sample geometries.
The Getting Started button leads to the install command and generated usage for the active configuration.
The CDN tab displays a different generated usage example in HTML.
The NPM tab restores the package-manager install command and JavaScript usage.
Selecting pnpm changes the generated install command to pnpm add.
The custom-style GeoJSON example settles with a world map, a red sample rectangle and the example source.
Returns from the custom-style example to the home page with Default Control and the default blue sample features.
The TerrainRGB elevation example opens with its fully loaded satellite map, measuring tools and source code.
The completed multi-vertex line on the TerrainRGB map gains its stable distance and elevation labels.
Returns from the terrain example to the home page’s Default Control sample map.
The custom-font measurement example settles with its pale world map, drawing tools and source code.
The completed line across Africa and Asia displays distance and altitude using the example’s custom font.
Returns from the custom-font example to the home page and settles on the Examples gallery.
Returns from the browser to the Live demo slide with the demo QR code.
Thank-you slide introduces the GitHub repository URL and QR code.
The GitHub repository settles with its file list, commit details, description, and release information.
Returns from GitHub to the thank-you slide.
The conference title card returns with the session details and GeoCat livestream sponsorship.
The opening conference attribution card returns with the Powered by OSGeo credit.
